As a project we need to sort out whether this is acceptable.

My preference is that you send support for the SoC upstream so we don't have to do this.

Thanks for the feedback. We plan to upstream AST2700 support, but it may take some time. We need this branch, or for OpenBMC’s U-Boot to support the 2023.10 release, to enable AST2700 bring-up and testing.

I've created this:

https://github.com/openbmc/technical-oversight-forum/issues/53

@vince_chang@aspeedtech.com I much rather we motivate the upstreaming effort with the bringup and testing needs. Can we get some initial platform support merged it at least gives us something to configure the build for in the OpenBMC tree.
Thanks, @andrew@codeconstruct.com.au. I'll discuss it with the development team and get back to you.
We will upstream the Linux changes first because some of the code are shared. After the Linux changes are accepted, we will upstream the U-Boot part.

By the project policy, u-boot maintenance follows the same philosophies as kernel maintenance. Please upstream the u-boot patches for us to backport.

https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/7d54ee958a7ff0635cde4af2c7cec8fd49455c9f/kernel-development.md#L3-L6

We understand the OpenBMC policy. Currently we are focusing on upstreaming the Linux kernel support. After that, we will upstream the shared/common functionality into U-Boot as well.

Before that work is completed, we still need this commit to validate the evb-ast2700 build.

I recommend you start the u-boot upstreaming process for the pieces that already have been accepted into the kernel. Strike while the iron's hot 😊

I expect the only contention will be the devicetree bindings, and again, agreement there from the kernel maintainers should be enough to unblock any related u-boot work.
